images.title: One solid, two different profiles
images.purpose: Shows a tent shaped triangular prism that looks like a triangle from the front and a rectangle from the side.
images.composition: Plain white background with generous empty margins; the main object is large and centred and fills about 60 percent of the frame; nothing else is drawn. Three items in one row: the triangle profile on the left, the prism in the centre, the rectangle profile on the right, with a thin grey arrow from the prism to each profile.
images.exact_structure: Centre: a triangular prism lying on a rectangular face like a tent, drawn flat with thin dark outlines, its triangular front face filled teal #0072B2 and its two sloping rectangular faces filled amber #E69F00; the front triangle faces left. Left: a flat teal triangle, the same size as the prism's triangular face, with 'from the front' under it. Right: a flat amber rectangle, as tall as the prism and as long as the prism, with 'from the side' under it. Two thin grey arrows: one from the prism to the triangle, one from the prism to the rectangle. Nothing else.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The same solid can look like a triangle from one side and a rectangle from another.
images.description: Shows a tent shaped triangular prism that looks like a triangle from the front and a rectangle from the side.
images.context: Concept T5.C2x; one image that shows only the main idea.
images.teaching_notes: A square pyramid also gives a triangle and a square (a rectangle with equal sides): solids are not unique.

image_decisions.why: Profiles are seen, not computed; one solid beside its two outlines shows the contrast directly.
